svg.title: Valet Key
svg.desc: Valet Key. Give clients a short-lived, narrowly scoped URL to read or write storage directly. Step 1, The API in the data path: Ana's 2 GB video streams through the API to storage: every byte, in and out, for minutes. Step 2, Ask for a key, not data: The API checks Ana may add videos, then signs a URL to write video-981.mp4 only, for 15 minutes. Step 3, Straight to storage: The upload goes straight to storage, which checks the key; a storage event sends it for scanning. Step 4, A leaked key does little: A copied URL can only write video-981.mp4 until it expires; reads and deletes are refused.

the API signs with its own
The API carries every byte, in and out
• one instance is tied up for minutes per upload
• it needs long timeouts and large buffers
• the API tier is scaled for bandwidth, not for its logic
The valet key: a URL the API signs for one job (schematic)
has a copy of the URL
Taking a key back early is the hard part
• keep lifetimes short: minutes, not days
• sign with credentials or a policy that you
can revoke, which cancels all its keys at once
a read-only URL for one object, also short-lived
